scope: ROOT CAUSE: the playerState block's history argument is NULL, which is the symptom of cgame not being fully initialised

the_call_site.0x47239A: test edi,edi ; je 0x47232B          -> if the history pointer is NULL, take a different path
the_call_site.0x4722E8: cmp [edi+0x3B88], eax             -> edi is a large client structure (the one holding +0x3BA0)
the_call_site.conclusion: arg3 is a client-side structure that the caller passes as NULL when the client is not fully in a map

the_circular_dependency: the ps field decode requires `current == last`, and `current` comes from that history structure
the history structure is NULL until the client is fully initialised (cgame up, map loaded)
a fully initialised client is exactly what this project has never achieved - the frame is black because cgame has no scene data
so: **no map load -> no history structure -> no field decode -> no playerState content -> (indirectly) no scene data**
and the loop closes: the world cannot be made visible by constructing a snapshot, because the snapshot's content path is gated behind the world already being loaded
why_earlier_results_looked_like_progress: an empty playerState parses fine (stream_error 0) and the client still reaches state 10, so every 'accepted' body was really 'empty ps accepted'
the field-write attempts added bits after the empty block, which the following blocks consumed - producing the inconsistent lengths and the crashes
what_this_means_for_the_next_phase: the real target is the MAP LOAD completion, not the snapshot content: until cgame initialises, no playerState field can ever be decoded
the load path was explored in the earlier rounds (0x8018B0 / 0x803830 / 0xB7A670 and the command-buffer route) and never completed - that is where the work must resume
a captured real snapshot would help only after the client is in a state where it parses snapshots with a valid history, so it does not bypass this dependency
